Incident INC-001: Checkout DB pool exhaustion during flash sale
Service: checkout
Severity: high
Symptoms: checkout requests began timing out; DB connection count reached pool maximum; API latency rose sharply after traffic increased
Root cause: Connection pool size remained at 20 while traffic increased 3x during a flash sale.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted checkout pods without changing pool configuration; Increased application CPU limits; Cleared Redis cache
Successful resolution steps: Raised DB pool max to 60 after confirming DB had capacity; Reduced connection leak by upgrading the DB client version; Added pool utilization alert
Resolution: Traffic surge exposed an undersized connection pool and a client-side connection leak. Increasing capacity and fixing the client leak restored normal checkout latency.
Postmortem: ['Avoid blindly restarting pods; the symptom returned.', 'CPU scaling did not address the exhausted DB connections.']
Tags: DB connection pool exhaustion, traffic spike, connection leak

Incident INC-002: Payments API database connection saturation
Service: payments-api
Severity: critical
Symptoms: payment requests timed out; active DB connections stayed at 100%; new requests queued behind existing connections
Root cause: A deployment changed transaction handling and connections were not released on one error path.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Scaled payments-api horizontally; Restarted the database; Raised request timeout
Successful resolution steps: Rolled back the deployment; Verified connections were released after rollback; Added connection leak test coverage
Resolution: A recent deployment introduced a connection-release regression. Rollback immediately reduced active connections and restored payment processing.
Postmortem: ['Horizontal scaling increased total connection pressure.', 'Database restart was avoided after rollback proved sufficient.']
Tags: DB connection exhaustion, bad deployment, connection leak

Incident INC-003: User service connection pool exhausted
Service: user-service
Severity: high
Symptoms: login/profile requests returned 500s; connection pool wait time increased; database CPU remained moderate
Root cause: The service used a pool size of 10 after a configuration change, below the normal production value of 40.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Increased pod replicas; Cleared application cache; Restarted one pod
Successful resolution steps: Restored pool size to 40; Confirmed pool wait time returned to baseline; Added configuration validation at startup
Resolution: A configuration change reduced the database connection pool from 40 to 10. Restoring the expected pool size resolved the failures.
Postmortem: ['Adding replicas did not solve the per-process pool limit.', 'Cache clearing had no effect on DB connection waits.']
Tags: DB connection exhaustion, config error, pool size

Incident INC-004: Reporting jobs consume all database connections
Service: reporting
Severity: medium
Symptoms: interactive reports became slow; scheduled jobs held many DB connections; connection wait time spiked during batch start
Root cause: A new reporting job opened many concurrent database sessions and did not cap concurrency.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted reporting workers; Increased web request timeout; Scaled the reporting service
Successful resolution steps: Capped reporting job concurrency at 5; Killed only the runaway batch workers; Added DB connection usage monitoring
Resolution: A reporting batch exceeded safe DB connection concurrency. Limiting worker concurrency released enough connections for interactive traffic.
Postmortem: ['Scaling reporting workers increased DB connection usage.', 'Timeout increases only hid the underlying contention.']
Tags: DB connection exhaustion, batch workload, concurrency

Incident INC-005: Checkout feature flag points to missing payment route
Service: checkout
Severity: high
Symptoms: checkout returned 404 after deployment; only users in the new checkout cohort were affected; application logs showed missing route errors
Root cause: A feature flag enabled a new payment route before the route was deployed to production.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Rolled back the entire application; Cleared CDN cache; Restarted checkout pods
Successful resolution steps: Disabled the feature flag; Verified route availability; Added flag-to-route deployment validation
Resolution: A feature flag activated functionality before its backend route existed. Disabling the flag restored checkout without a full rollback.
Postmortem: ['Pod restarts did not create the missing route.', 'CDN clearing was unrelated to the backend 404.']
Tags: feature flag, configuration error, missing route

Incident INC-006: Notification service missing environment variable
Service: notification
Severity: high
Symptoms: notification workers crash-looped; startup logs reported missing API endpoint; email delivery stopped after deployment
Root cause: The deployment omitted NOTIFICATION_PROVIDER_URL from the production environment.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Increased pod memory; Deleted and recreated pods; Changed retry count
Successful resolution steps: Compared deployment environment with the previous release; Restored NOTIFICATION_PROVIDER_URL; Added startup configuration validation
Resolution: The new deployment omitted a required environment variable. Restoring it allowed workers to start and process notifications.
Postmortem: ['Memory changes did not affect startup validation.', 'Retries could not help a process that never initialized.']
Tags: missing environment variable, deployment configuration, startup failure

Incident INC-007: Search service wrong feature flag causes empty results
Service: search
Severity: medium
Symptoms: search returned empty results for 20% of users; no database error was present; issue began immediately after flag rollout
Root cause: A ranking experiment flag selected an index alias that did not exist in production.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Reindexed the entire search cluster; Restarted search pods; Increased search timeout
Successful resolution steps: Disabled the experiment flag; Verified the index alias; Added flag rollout checks
Resolution: A feature flag selected a nonexistent search index alias. Disabling the flag restored results.
Postmortem: ['Full reindex was unnecessary.', 'Timeout tuning did not address the invalid alias.']
Tags: feature flag, index alias, configuration

Incident INC-008: Auth gateway missing JWT issuer variable
Service: auth-gateway
Severity: critical
Symptoms: all authenticated requests returned 401; gateway startup succeeded; JWT validation logs showed issuer mismatch
Root cause: JWT_ISSUER was changed in the deployment template but the corresponding production value was not updated.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Rotated all user passwords; Restarted gateway pods; Increased token TTL
Successful resolution steps: Compared current and previous deployment environment values; Restored the correct issuer; Added configuration drift detection
Resolution: A deployment configuration mismatch caused valid tokens to fail issuer validation. Restoring the expected issuer resolved authentication.
Postmortem: ['Password rotation did not address token validation.', 'Restarting pods loaded the same incorrect value.']
Tags: JWT issuer, environment variable, config drift

Incident INC-009: Checkout payment provider timeout cascade
Service: checkout
Severity: critical
Symptoms: checkout latency exceeded 10 seconds; payment provider calls timed out; checkout pods accumulated waiting requests
Root cause: The external payment provider experienced elevated latency and checkout had an overly long upstream timeout.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Scaled checkout pods; Increased application timeout; Restarted checkout pods
Successful resolution steps: Reduced provider timeout to 3 seconds; Enabled graceful fallback for payment status; Confirmed provider recovery
Resolution: A third-party payment provider was slow. Long upstream timeouts caused request pileups; a shorter timeout and fallback prevented the cascade.
Postmortem: ['Scaling pods increased concurrent waiting requests.', 'Longer timeouts worsened request accumulation.']
Tags: third-party timeout, cascade, upstream latency

Incident INC-010: Inventory API slow causes checkout timeouts
Service: checkout
Severity: high
Symptoms: checkout failures correlated with inventory calls; inventory p95 latency increased; database latency was normal
Root cause: Inventory API experienced a slow query after a data growth threshold.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Increased checkout timeout; Restarted checkout; Scaled checkout pods
Successful resolution steps: Confirmed inventory latency independently; Applied the optimized inventory query; Reduced checkout dependency timeout
Resolution: Checkout was healthy; its dependency on inventory was slow because of a query regression. Fixing the dependency query removed checkout timeouts.
Postmortem: ['Checkout scaling did not reduce dependency latency.', 'Increasing the timeout delayed failures.']
Tags: dependency timeout, slow query, cascade

Incident INC-011: Notification provider outage
Service: notification
Severity: high
Symptoms: email sends failed; provider API returned 503; internal notification queue grew
Root cause: Third-party email provider had an external service outage.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted notification workers; Rotated API credentials; Increased worker replicas
Successful resolution steps: Confirmed provider status and 503 response pattern; Paused noncritical retries; Resumed delivery after provider recovery
Resolution: The incident was caused by an external email provider outage. Internal restarts could not restore the provider; controlled retry behavior prevented queue amplification.
Postmortem: ['Credential rotation did not change provider 503s.', 'More workers increased retry pressure.']
Tags: third-party outage, 503, dependency failure

Incident INC-012: User service memory leak after release
Service: user-service
Severity: high
Symptoms: memory usage climbed steadily; pods were OOM-killed; issue began after a release
Root cause: A new profile serialization path retained large objects in memory.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Increased pod memory limit; Added more replicas; Cleared Redis
Successful resolution steps: Rolled back the release; Verified memory stabilized; Created heap profiling regression test
Resolution: A release introduced a memory leak in profile serialization. Rollback stopped the growth and restored stability.
Postmortem: ['More memory only delayed OOM kills.', 'Redis clearing did not change heap growth.']
Tags: memory leak, deployment, OOM

Incident INC-013: Search CPU spike from unbounded query
Service: search
Severity: high
Symptoms: search CPU reached 95%; latency increased; one query pattern dominated CPU profiles
Root cause: A newly enabled query allowed an expensive unbounded wildcard search.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Increased CPU limits; Restarted search pods; Scaled replicas
Successful resolution steps: Disabled the offending query pattern; Added query cost limits; Added CPU alert tied to query rate
Resolution: An unbounded wildcard query saturated search CPU. Restricting the query and adding cost controls restored latency.
Postmortem: ['Scaling delayed saturation but did not remove the expensive query.', 'CPU limit changes only postponed the problem.']
Tags: CPU spike, expensive query, resource exhaustion

Incident INC-014: Reporting worker memory growth
Service: reporting
Severity: medium
Symptoms: reporting workers consumed increasing memory; jobs slowed over time; workers eventually restarted
Root cause: A CSV export library retained generated rows until the whole job completed.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Increased worker memory; Reduced job timeout; Added more workers
Successful resolution steps: Changed export implementation to stream rows; Restarted workers after deployment; Added memory-per-job monitoring
Resolution: The export implementation accumulated the entire dataset in memory. Streaming rows removed the growth pattern.
Postmortem: ['More memory delayed failure.', 'Timeout changes did not reduce memory use.']
Tags: memory growth, batch job, resource exhaustion

Incident INC-015: Payment DNS resolution failures
Service: payments-api
Severity: critical
Symptoms: payment provider hostname intermittently failed to resolve; application logs showed DNS lookup errors; internal services remained healthy
Root cause: A DNS resolver configuration change introduced intermittent resolution failures for the payment provider domain.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted payment pods; Rotated payment credentials; Increased HTTP timeout
Successful resolution steps: Compared resolver configuration with baseline; Reverted DNS configuration; Added external DNS resolution checks
Resolution: An infrastructure DNS configuration change caused intermittent external hostname resolution failures. Reverting it restored payment traffic.
Postmortem: ['Application restarts could not fix resolver configuration.', 'HTTP timeout did not affect failed name resolution.']
Tags: DNS failure, network, external dependency

Incident INC-016: Auth gateway internal DNS outage
Service: auth-gateway
Severity: high
Symptoms: auth requests failed with upstream connection errors; service discovery names could not resolve; pods themselves were healthy
Root cause: A CoreDNS configuration rollout introduced an invalid upstream rule.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted auth pods; Scaled auth gateway; Changed application retry count
Successful resolution steps: Checked DNS resolution from inside a pod; Rolled back CoreDNS configuration; Verified service discovery
Resolution: An invalid CoreDNS rule broke service discovery. Rolling back the DNS configuration restored authentication traffic.
Postmortem: ['Scaling application pods did not repair DNS.', 'Retry increases added latency without fixing resolution.']
Tags: DNS failure, CoreDNS, service discovery

Incident INC-017: Expired TLS certificate on payment provider
Service: payments-api
Severity: critical
Symptoms: TLS handshake failures began at midnight; payment provider hostname was reachable; certificate validation failed
Root cause: The client trust path encountered an expired provider certificate that had not been renewed.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted payment service; Changed HTTP timeout; Rotated API key
Successful resolution steps: Verified certificate expiry; Escalated to provider and switched to the documented fallback endpoint; Added certificate expiry monitoring
Resolution: The payment provider certificate expired. The application was healthy; certificate validation blocked connections until the provider renewed the certificate/fallback was used.
Postmortem: ['Restarting did not change certificate validity.', 'API key rotation was unrelated to TLS validation.']
Tags: expired certificate, TLS, authentication

Incident INC-018: Auth tokens rejected due to clock skew
Service: auth-gateway
Severity: high
Symptoms: valid JWTs were rejected as expired; multiple auth pods showed different system times; issue appeared after node maintenance
Root cause: A subset of nodes had clock drift beyond the JWT tolerance window.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Rotated signing keys; Restarted all auth pods; Increased token lifetime
Successful resolution steps: Compared node clocks; Corrected NTP synchronization; Verified token acceptance across nodes
Resolution: Clock drift caused valid JWTs to appear expired. Restoring NTP synchronization fixed validation without changing token policy.
Postmortem: ['Key rotation would not fix time-based validation.', 'Longer token lifetime would mask the infrastructure issue.']
Tags: clock skew, JWT, NTP

Incident INC-019: Expired internal service certificate
Service: inventory
Severity: high
Symptoms: inventory service could not call catalog service; TLS verification failed; failure began after certificate expiry date
Root cause: An internal certificate renewal job failed silently.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted inventory pods; Changed service timeout; Disabled retries
Successful resolution steps: Confirmed certificate expiry; Renewed the certificate; Added renewal-job failure alerting
Resolution: A failed certificate renewal job left an internal TLS certificate expired. Renewal restored service communication.
Postmortem: ['Restarts loaded the same expired certificate.', 'Timeout changes were unrelated to TLS verification.']
Tags: expired certificate, certificate renewal, TLS

Incident INC-020: Database migration blocks startup
Service: user-service
Severity: critical
Symptoms: new pods fail startup health checks; migration lock remains held; old version pods continue serving
Root cause: A migration attempted to alter a large table synchronously during application startup.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted failed pods; Scaled the deployment; Increased startup timeout
Successful resolution steps: Stopped the migration job; Released the lock; Ran the migration using an online procedure
Resolution: A blocking schema migration prevented new application instances from becoming ready. The migration was rerun safely outside startup.
Postmortem: ['Scaling created more blocked pods.', 'Startup timeout only prolonged rollout time.']
Tags: migration failure, startup, database lock

Incident INC-021: Kubernetes pod crash from invalid liveness probe
Service: notification
Severity: medium
Symptoms: pods repeatedly restarted; application health endpoint returned 200 when called manually; Kubernetes events showed failed liveness probes
Root cause: The deployment used the wrong liveness probe path after a route rename.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Increased failure threshold; Added more replicas; Raised pod CPU limit
Successful resolution steps: Compared probe path with application routes; Corrected the liveness path; Rolled out one pod first
Resolution: Kubernetes restarted healthy notification pods because the liveness probe targeted a removed route. Correcting the probe fixed the restarts.
Postmortem: ['Resource changes did not affect the probe failure.', 'More replicas would have multiplied unnecessary restarts.']
Tags: Kubernetes, liveness probe, deployment

Incident INC-022: Redis cache outage increases database load
Service: checkout
Severity: high
Symptoms: cache hit rate dropped to near zero; database QPS doubled; checkout latency increased
Root cause: A Redis cluster failover left several cache shards unavailable.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Scaled checkout pods; Increased DB connection pool; Restarted checkout
Successful resolution steps: Confirmed Redis errors and cache miss increase; Restored Redis shard availability; Added cache degradation circuit behavior
Resolution: Redis shard unavailability caused a cache miss storm and increased database load. Restoring Redis reduced DB pressure.
Postmortem: ['Increasing DB pool could have worsened DB saturation.', 'Application restarts did not restore Redis.']
Tags: Redis failure, cache miss storm, database load

Incident INC-023: Payment API timeout from connection leak
Service: payments-api
Severity: critical
Symptoms: payment latency gradually increased; HTTP client connection count grew; timeouts increased over several hours
Root cause: A third-party HTTP client was not closing connections on failed requests.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted pods; Increased timeout; Scaled replicas
Successful resolution steps: Captured connection metrics; Deployed client patch that closes failed connections; Verified connection count stabilized
Resolution: A connection leak in the outbound HTTP client caused gradual resource exhaustion. The client patch fixed the leak.
Postmortem: ['Restarts were only temporary relief.', 'Longer timeouts increased resource retention.']
Tags: connection leak, HTTP client, resource exhaustion

Incident INC-024: Bad deployment config disables inventory writes
Service: inventory
Severity: high
Symptoms: inventory reads succeed; stock updates fail with 500; logs show database write mode disabled
Root cause: A deployment config set INVENTORY_WRITE_ENABLED=false in production.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted inventory pods; Cleared cache; Increased database capacity
Successful resolution steps: Compared environment configuration; Restored INVENTORY_WRITE_ENABLED=true; Added production config validation
Resolution: A deployment configuration accidentally disabled inventory writes. Restoring the flag recovered stock updates.
Postmortem: ['Database capacity was healthy.', 'Restarting pods did not change the environment value.']
Tags: deployment config, feature flag, write failure

Incident INC-025: Third-party fraud API outage
Service: payments-api
Severity: high
Symptoms: payments requiring fraud checks time out; fraud provider returns 502; non-fraud internal endpoints are healthy
Root cause: External fraud provider outage caused payment authorization requests to wait for downstream responses.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Scaled payments-api; Restarted payment pods; Increased downstream timeout
Successful resolution steps: Confirmed provider 502s; Enabled documented degraded-mode behavior for low-risk transactions; Reduced retry amplification
Resolution: The fraud provider was unavailable. The service used its approved degraded path and controlled retries until the provider recovered.
Postmortem: ['Scaling did not repair the external provider.', 'Longer timeouts increased request backlog.']
Tags: third-party outage, 502, dependency timeout

Incident INC-026: Search index corruption after node restart
Service: search
Severity: high
Symptoms: search results missing documents; index shard recovery loop observed; issue began after abrupt node restart
Root cause: A corrupted shard prevented normal index recovery.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Reindexed the whole cluster; Restarted all search nodes; Increased query timeout
Successful resolution steps: Isolated the affected shard; Restored the shard from snapshot; Verified document counts
Resolution: One search shard was corrupted after an abrupt node restart. Restoring only the affected shard avoided a full reindex.
Postmortem: ['Full cluster reindex was unnecessarily expensive.', 'Timeout changes did not repair the index.']
Tags: index corruption, snapshot restore, search

Incident INC-027: Webhook duplicate delivery after retry change
Service: payments-api
Severity: medium
Symptoms: merchant systems received duplicate payment webhooks; duplicates began after retry configuration change; payment records themselves were correct
Root cause: Webhook retry policy was changed without preserving idempotency keys across retries.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Disabled all webhooks; Restarted workers; Increased delivery timeout
Successful resolution steps: Restored idempotency-key propagation; Deduplicated queued events; Added duplicate-delivery test
Resolution: A retry configuration change dropped idempotency keys, allowing duplicate webhook delivery. Restoring the key propagation fixed duplicates.
Postmortem: ['Restarting workers did not change event identity.', 'Longer timeout did not address duplicate semantics.']
Tags: webhook retry, idempotency, configuration

Incident INC-028: Reporting database replica lag
Service: reporting
Severity: medium
Symptoms: reports show stale data; primary database is healthy; replica replication lag increased sharply
Root cause: A long-running analytical query on the read replica consumed resources and delayed replication.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted reporting service; Cleared application cache; Increased report timeout
Successful resolution steps: Identified the long-running replica query; Cancelled the offending query; Added replica-lag alerting
Resolution: Replica lag was caused by a resource-heavy analytical query. Removing the query restored replication freshness.
Postmortem: ['Application restart did not affect replica workload.', 'Timeout changes could not reduce replica lag.']
Tags: replica lag, database, long-running query

Incident INC-029: Checkout DNS failure caused by stale resolver cache
Service: checkout
Severity: high
Symptoms: checkout intermittently cannot resolve inventory hostname; only some pods affected; new pods are healthy
Root cause: A subset of nodes retained stale DNS resolver state after a service endpoint change.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Restarted checkout application; Scaled checkout pods; Increased inventory timeout
Successful resolution steps: Compared DNS resolution by node; Flushed node resolver cache; Verified consistent resolution
Resolution: Stale resolver state on a subset of nodes caused intermittent dependency lookup failures. Clearing resolver state restored consistency.
Postmortem: ['Application-level restarts did not clear the node resolver cache.', 'Timeout tuning did not affect DNS lookup.']
Tags: DNS failure, stale resolver, dependency

Incident INC-030: Authentication service unavailable after secret format change
Service: auth-gateway
Severity: critical
Symptoms: auth pods start but reject all tokens; secret parsing warnings appear; issue began immediately after secret rotation
Root cause: The signing secret was stored in a new encoded format but the application expected the previous representation.
Failed troubleshooting attempts: Rotated the secret again; Restarted all pods; Increased JWT tolerance
Successful resolution steps: Compared secret format between releases; Restored compatible secret representation; Added secret-format compatibility test
Resolution: A secret format change made the authentication service interpret the signing key incorrectly. Restoring the expected representation recovered token validation.
Postmortem: ['Another rotation would reproduce the same incompatible format.', 'Restarting pods only reloaded the incompatible secret.']
Tags: secret format, JWT, configuration
